item.title: 269220 : I-71 North-South between MM 0.1 and 2.0 Between I-64/I-71 Interchange and Zorn Ave. in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The I-71 widening and improvement project is a $50 million infrastructure investment to enhance safety and improve mobility along one of Louisville's most critical travel corridors. The two-year project, focused on increasing traffic capacity and safety, will enhance regional connectivity, provide reliable travel for years to come, and support economic growth. The project spans approximately two miles of interstate from the I-65/I-71 interchange near Frankfort Avenue to the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange. Additional improvements include the construction of a multi-use path along Zorn Avenue between the I-71/Zorn Avenue interchange and Mellwood Avenue, as well as a new median treatment at the intersection of Zorn Avenue and Mellwood Avenue to enhance safety and better define traffic movements. The project also includes the demolition and reconstruction of the I-71 bridge over Beargrass Creek, along with a latex overlay on the I-71 bridge over I-64 at mile point 0.3 to extend the structure’s service life. For additional information, please visit https://transportation.ky.gov/DistrictFive/Pages/I-71-Widening---Louisville-.aspx.

item.title: 292980 : I-71/75 North Ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Boulevard in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : (June 5, 2026) – Interstate 71/75 ramp closures and detours in Covington are needed to safely advance construction on the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project, which will add interstate lanes, better access, a new companion bridge and convert the existing bridge for local travel to improve safety and increase regional highway capacity. Temporary closures and detours will now begin on Monday, June 8, and will take place in multiple phases. On Monday, June 8, the following closures are expected to take place: I-71/75 northbound off-ramp to 12th Street/MLK Jr. Blvd. (0.0 - 0.28 mile points): this closure will remain in place through Summer 2027. Detour: Traffic will use the I-71/75 northbound 5th Street exit ramp, turn left (north) onto Philadelphia Street, then left onto 4th Street driving west to the I-71/75 southbound ramp to Pike Street. Turn left on to Pike Street, then right on to Simon Kenton Way, then left on to MLK Blvd. KYTC will provide further updates ahead of the closures to inform all road users via the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project website. [links-1.govdelivery.com] Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. For the most current information on road construction in Northern Kentucky, please visit the District 6 Roadshow [links-1.govdelivery.com] or the Driving Northern Kentucky Progress [links-1.govdelivery.com] website. item.title: 310577 : I-71/75 North-South between MM 188.5 and 191.7 Between Kyles Lane and Brent Spence Bridge in Kenton County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (Nov. 5, 2026) -- The traffic impacts for Wednesday, Nov. 5 as part of the ongoing electrical project for the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project have been adjusted. Work tonight (Thursday, Nov. 5), will include a double left lane closure on Interstates 71/75 northbound in the project area. A single left lane closure will take place at 8 p.m. This will shift to a double left lane closure beginning at 11 p.m. A single right lane closure on I-71/75 southbound will be in place beginning at 8 p.m. All lanes reopen by 5 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 6. Work is expected to continue with single left lane closure in both directions overnight as the project progresses. KYTC will provide updates if additional traffic impacts are required to complete the project. This electrical work is expected to be completed by Monday, Nov. 30. COVINGTON, Ky. (Sept. 25, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of nightly lane closures on Interstates 71/75 in Kenton County beginning Monday, Sept. 28. Crews will be performing electrical work as part of the ongoing Brent Spence Bridge Corridor project. This work will require a nightly northbound and southbound left lane closure from Kyles Lane (KY 1072) (188.52 mile point) to the Brent Spence Bridge (191.63 mile point), a distance of 3.11 miles. Both left lanes (northbound and southbound) will be blocked from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. All lanes will reopen by 5 a.m. No lane closures associated with this portion of the project will be in place from Thursday, Oct. 8 through Sunday, Oct. 11 due to BLINK. Weather permitting, this portion of the project is expected to be completed Friday, Oct. 23. Project schedules are subject to change due to inclement weather or other unforeseen circumstances. About the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project The Brent Spence Bridge Corridor Project is one of the nation’s most significant transportation transformations, spanning eight miles of I-71/75 in Kentucky and I-75 in Ohio. Construction will begin with the new companion bridge to the west of the Brent Spence Bridge and one mile of approach work in each state. In addition to the new bridge, the project will restripe the existing Brent Spence Bridge to carry local traffic; improve safety and reduce congestion by separating local and through travel; redesign ramp configurations throughout the corridor; and add new pedestrian and bicycle connections linking neighborhoods to jobs and transit. This once-in-a-generation investment will strengthen national freight movement, support local businesses and workforce growth, and enhance quality of life for the millions who rely on this critical corridor. The project team coordinates with all navigation apps so drivers can easily determine the best route from their starting point to their destination. For more information, visit brentspencebridgecorridor.com.

item.description: Construction / Road Work : Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of daily blasting operations on Interstate 64 West beginning Wednesday, Sept. 2. item.title: 312747 : I-275 West between MM 75.0 and 75.6 At I-471 in Campbell County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of upcoming lane closures on Interstate 275 in Campbell County beginning Thursday, Nov. 19. These lane closures are necessary to provide a safe area for crews to perform concrete repairs on a bridge deck. Beginning at 8 p.m. on Thursday, Nov. 19, crews will block the right lane on the ramp from I-471 southbound to I-275 westbound (0.0 to 0.42 mile points), a distance of 0.42 miles. Additionally, the right lane on I-275 westbound from the I-471 interchange (75 mile point) to south of the bridge overpass over Three Mile Road (KY 2238) (75.6 mile point), a distance of 0.6 miles. These lane closures will remain in place throughout the entirety of the project. The left two lanes on I-275 westbound will be maintained. These lane closures will be in place during the Friday morning and afternoon peak travel times. Plan ahead. Expect significant delays during peak hours. These 24/7 lane closures will remain in place after crews have completed the concrete repairs to allow the concrete to cure and to ensure a longer lasting repair. Weather permitting, this bridge maintenance project is expected to be completed Sunday, Nov. 22.

item.title: 312855 : I-264 East Ramp from U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Rd) in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of upcoming temporary traffic restrictions on U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) and Interstate 264 (Watterson Expressway) beginning Friday, Nov. 20. The temporary traffic restrictions will allow crews to prepare for and complete a traffic shift onto the newly constructed portion of the U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) bridge over I-264, with the traffic switch scheduled to take place on Monday, Nov. 23. The new roadway elevation is nearly three feet higher than the existing roadway, requiring pavement tie-in work to accommodate the traffic switch to the newly constructed U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) bridge. To minimize extended traffic impacts in the area, the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) and I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) Widening and Improvement Project [links-1.govdelivery.com] team have combined project construction phasing into a single approach. The schedule for upcoming temporary traffic impacts listed below takes into consideration the potential for inclement weather and the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday. Beginning Friday, Nov. 20, at 8 p.m. through Monday, Nov. 23, at 6 a.m. The I-264 East on-ramp from U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) will be closed. The I-264 West off-ramp to U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) at Exit 22 will be closed. Motorists will still be able to access KY 22 at Exit 22 and should detour by turning left onto Lime Kiln Lane to reconnect with either eastbound or westbound U.S. 42. By 6 a.m. on Monday, Nov. 23, traffic will be shifted onto the newly constructed portion of the U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) bridge over I-264. All temporary traffic restrictions associated with the traffic shift are expected to be lifted by 6 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 25. This traffic configuration will remain in place through the Summer of 2027 as crews advance construction on the remaining portion of the bridge. The upcoming traffic shift marks a significant project milestone, with construction on the $130 million project now more than halfway complete. Motorists should heed signage, use caution when traveling through the work zone, and plan ahead for travel delays.

item.title: 312868 : I-65 South between MM 135.0 and 134.5 Between College Street and St. Catherine Street in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : The Kentucky Street and Brook Street Bridge off-ramp from southbound Interstate 65 to St. Catherine Street (Exit 135) has been rebuilt and is ready to reopen to traffic next week, marking another project milestone for the I-65 Central Corridor project to upgrade nine aging bridges. To reopen the ramp, one lane will be closed on southbound I-65 between College and St. Catherine streets from Friday, Nov. 20 at 9 p.m. through Monday, Nov. 23 at 6.a.m. The new off-ramp is expected to reopen to traffic by 6 a.m. on Monday, Nov. 23. The off-ramp has been closed since May 2026 to allow crews to demolish the old ramp bridge spanning Kentucky Street and build a new one. Work to be Completed on Chestnut and Gray Streets Access is also reopening for travelers on Chestnut Street, now that partial demolition and bridge work is complete overhead. Chestnut Street under I-65 is expected to reopen to traffic by 6 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 22. On Gray Street, traffic remains detoured for a separate non-KYTC project in the area, but crews expect to complete I-65 Central Corridor work there on Friday, Nov. 20. Pedestrian access will remain open. No new local street or ramp closures are expected to begin this year. Intermittent lane closures are anticipated as work continues. Staying Informed Project information and updates can be found at I65CentralCorridor.com [links-1.govdelivery.com]. While on the site, users can sign up [links-1.govdelivery.com] to have project and traffic updates delivered to their inboxes or by text to their phones. Project updates are shared on KYTC District 5 (D5) Facebook [links-1.govdelivery.com] and X [links-1.govdelivery.com] pages.

item.title: 254857 : I-264 East-West between MM 21.5 and 22.9 Area of US-42 in Jefferson County
item.description: Construction / Road Work : UPDATE (March 23, 2026) – The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) advises motorists of overnight lane and ramp closures on Interstate 264 East and West (Watterson Expressway) beginning Tuesday, March 24, as part of the $130 million widening and improvement project of I-264 and U.S. 42 (Brownsboro Road) [links-1.govdelivery.com]. Beginning Tuesday, March 24, at 8 p.m., through Wednesday, March 25, at 6 a.m.: Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East and West between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Beginning Wednesday, March 25, at 8 p.m., through Thursday, March 26, at 6 a.m.: The I-264 East ramp to I-71 South will be closed. Motorists should continue on I-264 East, take I-71 North, then follow I-265 North to reconnect with I-71 South. Alternating lane closures will occur on I-264 East between mile markers 23 and 22 (from the I-264/I-71 split to U.S. 42/Brownsboro Road). Motorists should heed signage, use caution when traveling through the work zone, and plan ahead for travel delays. The highway improvement project is expected to be completed by the Fall of 2027. More details, including project timelines and traffic impacts [links-1.govdelivery.com], will be shared online as work progresses. Motorists are encouraged to sign up for email or text alerts [links-1.govdelivery.com] regarding weekly traffic impacts pertaining to the project.
